Court No. - 16

Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 1819 of 2023
Applicant :- Adarsh Agrahari
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Civil Secrt. Lko.

And Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Zia Ul Qayuim,Ajeet Pratap Singh,Syed Mohd. Afzal
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Vidyarthi,J.

1. Heard Sri Zia Ul Qayuim, the learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri Rajeev Kumar
Verma, the learned Additional Government Advocate appearing on behalf of the State and perused
the records.

2. The instant application has been filed by the applicant seeking anticipatory bail in F.I.R. bearing
Case Crime No.798 of 2021, under Sections 409, 420, 120B, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C., registered at Police
Station Gomti Nagar, District Lucknow.

3.  The aforesaid case has been registered on the basis of an F.I.R. lodged on 07.10.2021 against six persons, including the applicant describing him 'Vice Precident Jaguar' alleging that the informant had invested various amounts in Shine Infra Project Private Limited in the year 2019 in the name of himself and his family members, but upon maturity of the amount, when the investors presented post dated cheques handed over by the company, the same were returned unpaid by the Bank.

4. In the affidavit filed in support of the anticipatory bail-application, it has been contended that the applicant is innocent and he has falsely been implicated in the present case.
In para 37 of the affidavit, criminal history of the applicant of one case i.e. FIR No.707 of 2021 registered at Police Station Gomti Nagar, Lucknow, on similar allegations, has been mentioned.
5. The learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail but he could not dispute the aforesaid aspects of the matter.

It has been further stated that the applicant has not hold any principal position in Shine Infra Project Private Limited and in fact he himself is one of the victims of the fraud committed by the Company as he had also made investments of Rs.41.5 Lakhs in the Company, in return whereof a peace of land was purportedly sold to the applicant through sale deed dated 07.08.2014 but the applicant could not get possession of the land purportedly sold to him.

It has been mentioned in the affidavit that the applicant has made huge investment in the Company and the cheques handed over to him towards repayment of the amount have been returned by the bank for the reason 'insufficient fund'.
6.

Having considered the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the fact that even as per the allegations in the FIR the applicant did not hold any principal position in the Company and the applicant denies having hold any position, at all, in the Company; that the applicant himself claims to be victim of fraud of committed by the Company, I am of the view that the aforesaid facts are sufficient for making out a case for granting anticipatory bail to the applicant.
7. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
